meta.title: Operation of Magnetic Stirrer in Pharmaceutical Chemistry Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide continuous, controlled, flameless stirring of reaction mixtures, solvent systems, and chemical solutions in organic and pharmaceutical chemistry reactions.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Chemistry laboratory for all operations requiring continuous liquid mixing including dissolution of reactants, titration reactions, and preparation of standard solutions.
procedure: Place the magnetic stirrer on a stable, level bench surface away from strong external magnetic fields.
Choose a PTFE-coated magnetic stir bar (flea) appropriate to the vessel size: small oval flea for 50–100 mL beakers; larger cylindrical flea for 250–1000 mL vessels.
Drop the stir bar gently into the reaction vessel; place the vessel centrally on the magnetic stirrer plate.
Connect to power and switch on; slowly increase speed from zero using the speed control knob.
Confirm the stir bar rotates smoothly in a stable, concentric pattern before proceeding.
Set the optimal speed: 50–150 RPM for gentle mixing; 200–400 RPM for dissolving solids; 500–700 RPM for vigorous mixing.
Monitor stirring throughout the reaction — if the bar starts 'dancing' (erratic movement), immediately reduce speed to zero and restart slowly.
After the reaction, reduce speed to zero before switching off.
Use a magnetic stir bar retriever wand to remove the stir bar from the vessel.
Rinse the stir bar with appropriate solvent and distilled water; store separately.
Wipe the stirrer plate with a damp cloth; ensure no chemical residue remains.
precautions: Do not start at high speed — always increase speed gradually to prevent bar dancing.
Do not use with ferrous metal containers or near large permanent magnets.
For viscous solutions, use lower speeds — high speed with viscous media generates excessive heat.
Clean the stirrer plate after each use — corrosive chemicals will damage the surface.
Record all malfunctions (bar dancing, motor noise) in the equipment log for maintenance.
Inspect PTFE coating on stir bars regularly — chipped coating can contaminate reaction mixtures.
